findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name: 'shards' vs 'shard'
findings.body: Line 185 uses `tags={"shard": shard_tag}` for the `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` metric, but line 199 uses `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` (plural) for `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce`. This inconsistency makes it harder to query and correlate these metrics in dashboards and alerts, and is likely a typo. One of them should be renamed to match the other.

findings.title: time.sleep(0.1) is ineffective due to monkeypatch, making test potentially flaky
findings.body: The test monkeypatches `time.sleep` to a no-op (`lambda _: None`) at line 15, then calls `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62 with a comment saying 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change'. Because `time.sleep` is monkeypatched, this call does nothing—the test does not actually wait. The test relies on the flusher thread picking up the new `current_drift` value before `step.join()` sets the `stopped` flag, which is a race condition. Under CI load, the flusher thread may not be scheduled between the drift change and `join()`, causing intermittent test failures. A real sleep (e.g., using the original `time.sleep` saved before monkeypatching, or `threading.Event.wait`) should be used here.

findings.title: Dead code: _create_process_for_shard is defined but never called
findings.body: The method `_create_process_for_shard` (lines 127–132) is defined but never invoked anywhere in the codebase. It appears to be a leftover from an earlier design that considered per-shard process restarts. This dead code adds confusion about the intended restart granularity and should be removed.

findings.title: New SpansBuffer created on every process restart without closing the old one
findings.body: Each call to `_create_process_for_shards` (including restarts triggered by `_ensure_processes_alive`) creates a new `SpansBuffer(shards)` at line 93 and stores it in `self.buffers[process_index]`, replacing the previous buffer object. If `SpansBuffer` holds Redis connections, client instances, or other resources, these are silently leaked on each restart. With up to `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS = 10` restarts per process, this could accumulate leaked connections. The old buffer should be explicitly closed or its resources released before replacement.

findings.title: record_stored_segments called on flusher-process buffers instead of the main ingestion buffer
findings.body: In `submit()`, `record_stored_segments()` is called on each buffer in `self.buffers` (line 269–270). These are separate `SpansBuffer` instances created for the flusher subprocesses. However, spans are written via `process_batch` using the original `buffer` passed to `__init__` (in factory.py line 67). If `record_stored_segments` relies on local state updated during `process_spans` (e.g., in-memory tracking of recently stored segments), calling it on different buffer instances that never received `process_spans` calls will produce incorrect results. This was not an issue in the previous single-buffer design where the same object was used for both writing and flushing.
